meta.title: Asymptotic conjecture on bipartite Cayley index for groups
meta.source_name: Jia-Li Du, Yan-Quan Feng and Pablo Spiga, “On the existence and the enumeration of bipartite regular representations of Cayley graphs over abelian groups”, arXiv:2001.03916 (2020).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.03916

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

345149.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, let $B$ be a subgroup of $G$ having index $2$, and let $c(G,B)$ and $\vec{c}(G,B)$ denote the corresponding Cayley indices. The conjecture concerns all sufficiently large groups, meaning that there is a positive integer threshold $n$.

**Asymptotic bipartite Cayley-index conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $n$ such that, if $G$ is a group of order at least $n$ and $B$ is a subgroup of $G$ having index $2$, then either $c(G,B)=1$, or there exists $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ with $\alpha\ne 1$, $B^\alpha=B$ and

$$
G=B\cup\{g\in G\mid g^\alpha=g\}\cup\{g\in G\mid g^\alpha=g^{-1}\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that, apart from the stated automorphism obstruction, sufficiently large groups and their index-$2$ subgroups admit the desired Cayley-index-$1$ structure. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

meta.title: Asymptotic locating chromatic number conjecture for regular palms
meta.source_name: Yusuf Hafidh and Edy Tri Baskoro, “On the Locating Chromatic Number of Trees”, arXiv:1912.05775 (2020).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05775

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

344875.statement:
Let $S_n(k)$ be the regular palm with $n$ arms, each having length $k$, and let $\chi_L(S_n(k))$ denote its locating chromatic number. **Asymptotic locating chromatic number conjecture.** For $k\geq 4$,

$$
\chi_L(S_n(k))=(1+o(1))\left(\frac{k-1}{2}\right)\sqrt[k]{4n}.
$$

This conjecture proposes the asymptotic order, including the leading constant, of the locating chromatic number of regular palms when the arm length is at least four. Exact formulas are established in the paper for arm lengths $k=1,2,3$, while the asserted asymptotic formula for $k\geq4$ remains open.

meta.title: The conjecture on cycle-free partial transversals of Latin squares
meta.source_name: Andras Gyarfas and Gabor N. Sarkozy, “Rainbow matchings and partial transversals of Latin squares”, arXiv:1208.5670 (2012).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.5670

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2012).

324028.statement:
A **Latin square of order $n$** is an $n\times n$ array in which every symbol occurs exactly once in each row and column. A **cycle-free partial transversal** is a partial transversal containing no cycles, where a cycle is a sequence of selected entries whose row and column indices form a cyclic pattern with all row and column indices distinct. **Cycle-free partial-transversal conjecture.** Any Latin square of order $n$ has a cycle-free partial transversal of order $n-2$.

The claim would strengthen the preceding asymptotic result by giving a cycle-free partial transversal missing at most two entries. The supplied text presents it as a possible strong form and gives no resolution status.

meta.title: Polynomial χ-bounds for forest-free graphs
meta.source_name: N. Rahimi and D. A. Mojdeh, “Towards Esperet's Conjecture: Polynomial χ-Bounds for Structured Graph Classes”, arXiv:2512.09186 (2025).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.09186

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2025). “This conjecture has been confirmed for some special trees (see, for example, ), but remains open in general.”

371954.statement:
Let $H$ be a forest, and let $G$ be an $H$-free graph, meaning that $G$ has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. Write $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number and $\omega(G)$ for its clique number. **Polynomial χ-bound conjecture for forest-free graphs.** There exists a constant $c>0$, depending on $H$, such that

$$
\chi(G)\leq \omega(G)^c
$$

for every $H$-free graph $G$. This conjecture is presented as a consequence of combining the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture with Esperet's conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

meta.title: Single-survivor conjecture for competing urns on hypercubes and discrete tori
meta.source_name: Daniel Ahlberg and Carolina Fransson, “Multi-colour competition with reinforcement”, arXiv:2206.00400 (2022).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00400

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

354845.statement: Let $K\ge3$, let the underlying graph be either a hypercube or a discrete torus, and let the initial configuration be any nonzero configuration of the $K$-type competing urn scheme. **Single-survivor conjecture.** The process has almost surely a single surviving type. The path and cycle are the only finite connected graphs known in the source to have this property for every $K\ge3$, while coexistence is known on some other graphs; the conjecture remains open for hypercubes and discrete tori.

meta.title: Rational exponent conjecture for the bipartite subdivision function
meta.source_name: Zixiang Xu and Gennian Ge, “On color isomorphic subdivisions”, arXiv:2009.01074 (2020).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.01074

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2020).

347828.statement:
Let $r\in(1,2)$ be rational. For a bipartite graph $H$, let $f_2(n,H)$ denote the corresponding bipartite subdivision function. **Rational exponent conjecture.** For every rational number $r\in(1,2)$, there exists a single bipartite graph $H$ such that

$$
f_2(n,H)=\Theta(n^r).
$$

The analogous rational exponent conjecture for the classical Turán function is open, and the paper notes that known results suggest a similar phenomenon for $f_2(n,H)$; determining whether every rational exponent in $(1,2)$ occurs remains open.

meta.title: Conjectures on complete hyperenergeticity of random graphs
meta.source_name: Octavio Arizmendi, Jorge Fernandez Hidalgo and Oliver Juarez-Romero, “Energy of a Vertex”, arXiv:1805.05483 (2018).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.05483

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

339249.statement: Let a graph be **completely hyperenergetic** when every vertex has energy exceeding the corresponding hyperenergetic threshold, and let a uniform random graph on $n$ points and a random $d$-regular graph be sampled as indicated. **Random-graph complete-hyperenergeticity conjectures.** (1) A uniform random graph on $n$ points is asymptotically almost surely not completely hyperenergetic. (2) A $d$-regular graph is almost surely completely hyperenergetic for $d\geq 7$. These conjectures concern the behavior of vertex energy across all vertices rather than only its typical value. The paper notes that random-matrix results readily give information about typical vertices, whereas properties holding for all vertices are more difficult; the conjectures are presented as open questions.

meta.title: The Potts occupancy conjecture for regular graphs
meta.source_name: Yufei Zhao, “Extremal regular graphs: independent sets and graph homomorphisms”, arXiv:1610.09210 (2017).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09210

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2016). “The conjecture remains open for all $d\ge 4$ and $q \ge 3$.”

334450.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, let $q\ge 3$ be an integer, and let $\beta>0$. For a coloring $\sigma:V(G)\to[q]$, let $m(\sigma)$ be the number of monochromatic edges, define

$$
Z_G^q(\beta)=\sum_{\sigma:V(G)\to[q]}e^{-\beta m(\sigma)},
$$

and set

$$
U_G^q(\beta)=-\frac{1}{v(G)}\frac{d}{d\beta}\log Z_G^q(\beta).
$$

**Potts occupancy conjecture.** For every $d$-regular graph $G$, every integer $q\ge 3$, and every $\beta>0$,

$$
U_G^q(\beta)\ge U_{K_{d,d}}^q(\beta).
$$

Consequently,

$$
Z_G^q(\beta)^{1/v(G)}\le Z_{K_{d,d}}^q(\beta)^{1/(2d)}.
$$

The conjecture would imply the proper-coloring inequality by taking the zero-temperature limit; it is presented as an open strengthening.

meta.title: Sigma clique covering growth conjecture for complete multipartite graphs
meta.source_name: Akbar Davoodi, Ramin Javadi and Behnaz Omoomi, “Sigma clique covering of graphs”, arXiv:1503.02380 (2015).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02380

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2015). “The problem that $ \cp(K_t(2))\sim 2t $ is still an open problem.”

330067.statement:
For positive integers $t$ and $d$, let $K_t(d)$ denote the complete $t$-partite graph with each part of size $d$. Let $f$ be a function and let $c$ be a constant.

**Sigma clique covering growth conjecture.** For every positive integers $t$ and $d$, if $t\geq f(d)$, then

$$
\operatorname{scc}(K_t(d))\geq cd^2t\log t.
$$

The conjecture would make the known upper bound for $\operatorname{scc}(K_t(d))$ sharp up to a constant factor for sufficiently large $t$. It is proved in the source for $d=2$, while the general case remains open.

meta.title: The chromatic extremal conjecture for regular graphs
meta.source_name: David Galvin, “Three tutorial lectures on entropy and counting”, arXiv:1406.7872 (2014).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7872

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2014). “This is open for all $q \geq 3$.”

328248.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex, $d$-regular graph, let $K_q$ be the complete graph on $q$ vertices, and let ${\rm hom}(G,K_q)$ denote the number of graph homomorphisms from $G$ to $K_q$. **Chromatic extremal conjecture.** For every $n$, $d$ and $q$,

$$
{\rm hom}(G,K_q)\leq {\rm hom}(K_{d,d},K_q)^{n/2d}.
$$

Equivalently, the number of proper $q$-colorings satisfies $c_q(G)\leq c_q(K_{d,d})^{n/2d}$. The conjecture is open for all $q\geq3$; it is known when $q=q(n,d)$ is sufficiently large, but the cited methods do not settle constant $q$.

meta.title: Faithfulness of regular Stanley sequences to their cores
meta.source_name: David Rolnick, “On the classification of Stanley sequences”, arXiv:1408.1940 (2014).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.1940

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

328539.statement: Let $S(A)=\{a_n\}$ and $S(A')=\{a'_n\}$ be Stanley sequences. Say that $S(A)$ is **faithful** to $S(A')$ if, for every $a'_n<\omega(A')$, there is an index $m$ such that $a_m=a'_n$. For a regular sequence, its core is denoted $S'(A)$. **Faithfulness conjecture.** Every regular Stanley sequence is faithful to its core. This proposed property would describe how the initial portion of a regular sequence retains the elements of its core; the source gives no proof or resolution.

meta.title: Adjacency perfect state transfer conjecture for trees
meta.source_name: Gabriel Coutinho and Henry Liu, “No Laplacian Perfect State Transfer in Trees”, arXiv:1408.2935 (2014).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2935

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

328573.statement: Let $T$ be a tree, let $P_2$ and $P_3$ denote the paths on two and three vertices, and say that $T$ has **adjacency perfect state transfer** if its adjacency-matrix continuous-time quantum walk transfers a state between two vertices with fidelity equal to $1$. **Adjacency perfect state transfer conjecture.** No tree except for $P_2$ and $P_3$ admits adjacency perfect state transfer. The paper establishes this for trees with a perfect matching and reports computational verification for all trees up to ten vertices, but leaves the general case open.

meta.title: The Stanley–Wilf conjecture for hereditary properties of tournaments
meta.source_name: József Balogh, Béla Bollobás and Robert Morris, “Hereditary properties of tournaments”, arXiv:math/0702371 (2007).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702371

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2007).

380420.statement:
Let $cmathcal{P}$ be a hereditary property of tournaments, and let $cmathcal{P}_n$ denote the tournaments in $cmathcal{P}$ on $n$ vertices. There exists a constant $calpha>0$ and a function $F(n)=n^{calpha n+o(n)}$ such that, for every hereditary property of tournaments $cmathcal{P}$, either

$$
|\mathcal{P}_n|\leq c^n
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and some constant $c=c(\mathcal{P})$, or

$$
|\mathcal{P}_n|\geq F(n)
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This conjectures a jump from exponential to factorial speed; the paper presents it as a tournament analogue of the Stanley–Wilf conjecture, and the general assertion remains open.

meta.title: The higher-residue conjecture for the VC-dimension of Cayley graphs
meta.source_name: Brad Rodgers and Anurag Sahay, “The VC-dimension of random subsets of finite groups”, arXiv:2506.14219 (2025).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14219

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

368882.statement:
Fix an integer $r\geqslant 3$. For primes $N\equiv 1\pmod r$, let $S\subseteq(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ be the multiplicative subgroup of $r$-th powers, and let $\Gamma=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z},S)$ be the Cayley graph with respect to the additive group of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. The **VC-dimension** $\operatorname{VCdim}(\Gamma)$ is the maximum cardinality of a set shattered by the neighborhoods of $\Gamma$.

**Higher-residue conjecture.** As $N\to\infty$ through the primes congruent to $1$ modulo $r$,

$$
\operatorname{VCdim}(\Gamma)=(1+o(1))\log_r N.
$$

The conjecture is presented as an alternative to the cited McDonald–Sahay–Wyman prediction involving base $2$. The source also expects a natural generalization over finite fields, but that expectation is not itself included as a separate conjecture.

meta.title: Katona–Xiao conjecture for the path-and-clique Turán problem
meta.source_name: Xiaona Fang, Xiutao Zhu and Yaojun Chen, “Generalized Turán problem for a path and a clique”, arXiv:2409.10129 (2024).
meta.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2312.00620](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00620).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10129

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

364797.statement:
Let $P_k$ be a path on $k$ vertices, let $K_m$ be the complete graph on $m$ vertices, and let $T(n,r)$ denote the Turán graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at most $r$. Write $I_s$ for the edgeless graph on $s$ vertices, $\delta_k$ for the relevant path parameter, and $G\vee H$ for the join of graphs $G$ and $H$. Assume $m+1\leq k\leq 2m-1$.

**Katona–Xiao conjecture.** If $k$ is odd and $(k-1)\mid n$, then the disjoint union of $n/(k-1)$ copies of $T(k-1,m-1)$ gives the maximum number of edges in a graph containing neither $P_k$ nor $K_m$, while for even $k$, $T(\delta_k,m-2)\vee I_{n-\delta_k}$ is extremal for sufficiently large $n$.

This conjecture concerns the remaining range $m<k\leq 2m-1$ in the generalized Turán problem forbidding both a path and a clique. The corresponding connected and unrestricted extremal values are known when $k>2m-1$, but this intermediate range remains unresolved.

meta.title: Generalized planar Turán conjecture for cycles with forbidden even cycles
meta.source_name: Ervin Győri, Addisu Paulos, Nika Salia, Casey Tompkins and Oscar Zamora, “Generalized Planar Turán Numbers”, arXiv:2002.04579 (2020).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.04579

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

345483.statement:
Let $\ell$ be a positive integer, and let $C_k$ denote the cycle of order $k$. For a graph $H$ and a forbidden family $\mathcal{F}$, let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,H,\mathcal{F})$ be the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no graph in $\mathcal{F}$ as a subgraph.

**Generalized cycle-count conjecture.** For sufficiently large $k$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,C_k,\{C_4,C_6,\dots,C_{2\ell}\})=\Theta\left(n^{\left\lfloor\frac{k}{\ell+1}\right\rfloor}\right).
$$

This extends the paper's established order of magnitude for cycles in $C_4$-free planar graphs and concerns the effect of forbidding the even cycles $C_4,C_6,\ldots,C_{2\ell}$. The statement is posed as open; the threshold implicit in “sufficiently large” is not specified in the source.

meta.title: Conjecture on the maximizing configuration for path graphs
meta.source_name: Antal A. Járai, “Phase transition in a sequential assignment problem on graphs”, arXiv:1507.04169 (2016).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.04169

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

330915.statement:
Let $G$ be a path with $k-1$ edges, where $k\geq 3$. For a configuration $\mathbf{n}^{\max}=(n^{\max}_j:j=1,\dots,k-1)$ in $n\,\mathcal{S}_G$ maximizing $p_G(\mathbf{n})$, define

$$
a_*(j;k)=\frac{\log\left(\frac{k-j-1}{k-j}\right)}{\log\left(\frac{j(k-j-1)}{(j+1)(k-j)}\right)},\qquad 1\leq j\leq k-2,
$$

with $a_*(0;k)=0$ and $a_*(k-1;k)=1$. **The maximizing-configuration conjecture.** For $1\leq j\leq k-2$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^j n^{\max}_\ell=a_*(j;k).
$$

The preceding results show that maximizers have success probability $c_G+o(1)$, but do not determine their location within an $o(n)$ neighborhood of the critical surface. This conjecture predicts that, after rescaling by $1/n$, the maximizing configuration converges to a specific interior point characterized by the displayed large-deviation expression; it remains unproved in the source.

meta.title: Explicit polynomial directed-clique construction conjecture for tournaments
meta.source_name: Grzegorz Gutowski and Mikołaj Rams, “A Note on the Complexity of Directed Clique”, arXiv:2602.11773 (2026).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

373109.statement:
Let $T_1,T_2,\ldots$ be tournaments, and write $V(T_n)$ for the vertex set of $T_n$. **Explicit tournament construction conjecture.** There is an explicit construction of tournaments $T_1,T_2,\ldots$ such that

$$
|V(T_n)|=\Theta(n)
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T_n)=\Omega(n^{1/100}).
$$

Such a construction would substantially improve the currently discussed logarithmic lower bounds for directed clique number in tournaments; its existence is left open by the source.

meta.title: The exponential growth-rate limit for planar spanning-tree values
meta.source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Alex Kontorovich and Igor Pak, “Spanning trees and continued fractions”, arXiv:2411.18782 (2025).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18782

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

365985.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the set of spanning-tree numbers $\tau(G)$ attained by simple planar graphs on $n$ vertices. The paper proves exponential lower and upper bounds for $|\mathcal T(n)|$. **Growth-rate limit conjecture.** There is a limit

$$
\gamma:=\lim_{n\to\infty}|\mathcal T(n)|^{1/n}.
$$

The conjectured limit would satisfy the bounds $1.49\leq\gamma\leq 5.2852$ from the cited estimates. The source presents existence of the limit as a natural conjecture; no resolution is given.

meta.title: Linial–Morgenstern minimum 4-cycle-density conjecture for tournaments
meta.source_name: Jie Ma and Tianyun Tang, “Minimizing cycles in tournaments and normalized q-norms”, arXiv:2011.14142 (2020).
meta.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14142

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

348815.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament, and let $t(C_{\ell},T)$ denote the number of homomorphisms from the directed cycle $C_{\ell}$ to $T$ divided by $|V(T)|^{\ell}$. A **random blow-up** of an $m$-vertex transitive tournament is a tournament whose vertex set is partitioned into parts $V_1,\ldots,V_m$, with arcs inside each part oriented randomly and all arcs between $V_i$ and $V_j$ oriented from $V_i$ to $V_j$ whenever $i<j$. Let $g_4:[0,1/8]\to[0,1]$ be the continuous increasing function defined by the random blow-up formula in the source. **Linial–Morgenstern's conjecture.** Every tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
t(C_4,T)\geq g_4(t(C_3,T))+o(1),
$$

where $o(1)\to0$ as $|V(T)|\to\infty$. The conjecture was proved for $t(C_3,T)\in[1/72,1/8]$, and is also known asymptotically at several endpoint values; the full range is not established in the supplied text.
